title: Monthly flow adjustment left the Delaware tidal-range contrast trend positive in 1990-2025
abstract: We tested whether monthly Delaware River flow at Trenton explains the rise in Philadelphia-minus-Cape May mean tidal range. We used 421 accepted months from 1990 to 2025. A month, time and 18.61-year cycle model gave a trend of 34.21 mm per decade. Adding log monthly mean flow gave 34.34 mm per decade, with conditional 95% five-year block limits of 27.34 to 41.17. The baseline-minus-adjusted difference was -0.131 mm per decade, with limits -0.784 to +0.570. Quadratic, seasonal and lagged flow terms also left positive adjusted trends. The simple flow slope was uncertain. These tests show that the tested flow adjustments did not explain the tide contrast trend. They do not identify channel change or exclude other river-tide effects. One flow gauge, two tide gauges, monthly averaging, short records, missing months and conditional error assumptions limit inference. Code, source hashes, monthly aggregates, draws, checks and a figure are included.

display.caption: Observed and flow-adjusted annual range contrasts, and monthly-model trend estimates with conditional five-year block intervals. The adjustment does not remove the positive trend.
